On your turn, you either take a card or pay a chip. Simple, right? But there's a catch: your cards count against you. Will you spend your limited supply of chips to avoid taking a card? Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary For tips on how to play no thanks, see Tips_nothanks Contents 1 Overview 2 Setup 3 Play 4 Scoring 4.1 Example 5 Variants Overview The goal of No Thanks! is to be the player with the fewest points when all cards are taken. In the BGA adaptation, points are negative, and the winner is the player whose score is closest to 0. Setup Each player receives 11 chips (3-5 players), 9 chips (6 players), 7 chips (7 players). Nine cards are removed from the deck (of cards numbered 3-35) at random. The top card of the deck is revealed. Play On your turn, you may spend a chip or take the card along with all of the chips in the pile. If you spend a chip, your turn ends. If you take the card, the next card is revealed, and your turn continues. The game ends when the last card is taken. Scoring Your score is the sum of your cards minus the number of chips you have. However, if you have cards with consecutive numbers, only the lowest number is added to your score. Example You have 5 chips and cards 3, 10, 11, 12, 13, and 20. Your score is 3 + 10 + 20 - 5 = 28. The player with the lowest score is the winner. Note: BGA calculates the scores as a negative. This means that the highest score (closest to 0) is the winner, and not the player with the most negative points. Variants Chip tracking: You can choose whether the amount of chips are visible throughout the game. Tactical Variant: Each player starts with 10 chips instead of 11. However, cards 10, 20 and 30 are guaranteed to be removed. [Rating: 1/10] Can't believe this is a game that so many people liked and talked about by famous reviewers.  So I bought it, tried it. Tried it with a different group. Different age. Different timing.......  Can't say anything more than just an exercise of taking cards or putting down a token as being fun.   The calculation of the score after the game was even more annoying.....up to the level of extreme hatred. Coupled with minus points from tokens made it even worst....no one else cared if anyone won or lost....  No thanks.....it's out the window as garbage.....

[Rating: 1/10] Classic filler auction game about bidding to not take points. It's an undeniably fun push your luck game, but that fun has an expiration date as after enough plays with a group of rational actors the mind games start to disappear and the pure luck of the draw becomes more prominent. Definitely a blast for those first couple of plays, but I see nothing appealing about it to comeback to.

[Rating: 2/10] I'd rather talk to people for the 5 minutes we would otherwise spend playing. Boring.

[Rating: 2/10] There isn't much 'game' here; it is one simple mechanic, repeated endlessly. The game might improve if played for actual money rather than chips. Schacht's Mogul employs a similar mechanic but includes a game with the box.

[Rating: 2/10] The name says it all!  In my book this is an NRF card game. (No Redeeming Features).

[Rating: 2/10] Bid for cards to score, while managing your dwindling pile of coins.  It always feels like you are losing, and trying to hopelessly not end up being coin-less. When you are winning, it doesn't feel rewarding. When you are losing, it feels like there is no hope of catching up.
